events.what: Briggs & Wells prove a 1.36π lower bound on the area of arbitrary isometric fillings of a length-2π circle via a discrete analogue
Chen, Li & Zhong improve the universal lower bound to 14ζ(3)/π ≈ 1.706π, stronger for orientable fillings, via a Fourier-coefficient method
Upper bound for discrete isometric filling of cycles; states it cannot settle Gromov's conjecture

judgement.doubts: Both bounds are unreviewed 2026 preprints. Chen–Li–Zhong improves the same quantity Briggs–Wells bounded, so it supersedes it as the event. The record gives the Chen–Li–Zhong authors by surname only.

outcome_prefix: Chen, Li & Zhong (arXiv:2609.08251, 8 Sep 2026) raise the lower bound for arbitrary isometric fillings to 14ζ(3)/π, beating the Briggs–Wells 1.36π bound.

corrections.why: F14: a progress row settles nothing, so it has no direction. The record says both papers 'do not resolve the conjecture'.
F8: the furthest event wins (§4 step 3). The record says Chen, Li & Zhong 'improved this to 14ζ(3)/π', so their result supersedes the Briggs–Wells bound on the same quantity.
F8: the credit follows the event the status rests on. The record gives these authors by surname only.
